newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris thanks Yeltsin, Primakov on NATO-Russia pact.
newsitem.headline: Paris thanks Yeltsin, Primakov on NATO-Russia pact.

text.p: France on Friday hailed an historic pact between NATO and Russia as vital to European security after the Cold War.
France, which is to host a ceremony in Paris on May 27 to sign the accord, also praised the contributions of Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.

"By this agreement, the two former adversaries (Russia and NATO) are turning the page on an era of confrontation and division, and are beginning a new relationship of confidence and cooperation, to the benefit of Europe's overall stability," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
"Russia's place in the new security architecture of Europe is thus definitively confirmed," Rummelhardt said.
The NATO-Russia "Founding Act" is intended to defuse Russian opposition to NATO's planned expansion into states in Eastern Europe that once formed part of the Soviet bloc.
The deal was approved by NATO's 16 member states on Friday after it was hammered out in Moscow this week by Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana after months of tough talks.

France thanked Yeltsin for his "far-reaching views, uncommon courage and determination" and Primakov for his skill in negotiating. Rummelhardt said France thanked Solana for his role in reaching an agreement "giving full satisfaction to all".
